name: Sodium-Ion Batteries: India's First Listed Cell & Pack Developers
scope: Sodium-ion cells (lithium-free, soda-ash/hard-carbon based) are moving from lab to pilot in India for stationary storage and data centres (Tata Chemicals' first Na-ion pack in test with a pilot due in 6-9 months per its Jul 2026 Q1 FY27 call; KPIT's licensed Na-ion technology; Oct 2026 Rajasthan 250 kW and NTPC Na-ion storage pilots); most Indian activity is in unlisted startups, so listed exposure is very narrow (2 large/mid caps, no small cap confirmed), neither stock has re-rated on this theme, and mainstream stock-pick coverage is minimal - early, but a small, long-dated option rather than a near-term earnings driver.
questions: What is sodium-ion battery technology, how does it differ from Li-ion (cost, energy density, safety, cycle life, cold performance), and which applications (stationary storage, data centres, 2/3-wheelers) is it realistically suited to?
What does current global market-research and trade press say about Na-ion commercialisation (China capacity, pricing vs LFP) and when does it reach cost parity?
What is India's policy and demand backdrop - ACC PLI chemistry neutrality, MNRE/NTPC/Rajasthan Na-ion storage pilots, BESS tenders - and how large could the addressable stationary-storage market be?

What exactly has Tata Chemicals disclosed on sodium-ion (pack built, pilot timeline, scale-up plan, soda ash/material linkage, capex), and how material could it be relative to its soda-ash and specialty business?

What is KPIT's sodium-ion role (technology developed with IISER Pune, licence to Trentar for a 3 GWh plant, royalty terms), what is the latest status of the Trentar plant, and how material is the revenue potential?

Are there any other NSE/BSE-listed companies with company-confirmed sodium-ion activity (cells, hard carbon anodes, cathode materials, packs, BESS integrators) - small and mid caps included - and which unlisted players (Naxion, Rechargion, Indi Energy, Epsilon) could list or partner with listed firms?
How have TATACHEM and KPITTECH traded over the last 6-12 months, and is any of it attributable to sodium-ion; how much broker or mainstream media coverage names these stocks as a sodium-ion group?

What are the key risks - Li-ion/LFP price declines, Chinese Na-ion scale, slow pilot-to-commercial conversion, small materiality to the parent's earnings, technology licensing dependence on an unlisted partner?

What upcoming catalysts exist (Tata Chemicals pilot completion and customer test units by end-FY27, Trentar plant milestones, Rajasthan/NTPC pilot awards, ACC PLI or BESS-VGF tweaks, Naxion 2026 cell plant)?
Which companies are supported only by technical adjacency (inference) rather than company statements, and should be watched but not included?

cell_and_pack_builders: Listed companies that have built sodium-ion packs or are piloting cell/pack manufacturing
technology_licensors: Listed companies that developed sodium-ion cell technology and are commercialising it via licensing partners
